Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our DPA for a pilot and need a few clarifications on notification and cooperation language before legal will sign. Two quick areas:

1) Timing: For GDPR controllers we typically expect notification "without undue delay and no later than 72 hours" after becoming aware. Can Redwood commit to that across EU data for both Hosted and Dedicated deployments? Can you confirm what "becoming aware" means operationally for you (ops alert, confirmed incident, etc.)?

2) Cooperation & evidence: We need an explicit commitment to cooperate with controller/regulator investigations and provide evidence (audit logs, flow records, SOC 2 evidence) within a reasonable period. Customers ask for a max window for initial evidence handover — is 10 business days realistic? Also we need to understand exceptions for law enforcement requests and subsidiaries in non-EU territories.

Attached is our standard notification clause and the SCCs redline — please confirm any material conflicts. We're also filling the SIG but flagged these items.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_SCCs_2027.docx, SIG-Questionnaire.pdf

Appreciate a short (bullet) reply we can share with counsel.

Best,

Jordan — thanks, got this. Short answers up front and then a proposed clause below. I"ll loop in Irene for SCC/legal nuance.

- Timing: We can accept "without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware" subject to two practical clarifications: (1) "becoming aware" = the time our security team reasonably confirms an incident affecting customer data (we can detect anomalous activity earlier via alerts but we generally wait until triage confirms data impact), and (2) operational constraints (forensic work or law enforcement preservation requests) may require a short pause on some disclosures.

- Evidence & cooperation: We are prepared to cooperate with controller and regulator investigations and to deliver initial evidence (audit logs, flow records, activity summaries) within 10 business days in typical cases. For deeper forensic exports or full packet captures there may be additional lead time; we propose a commitment to make available a prioritized evidence package in 10 business days and to continue producing additional artifacts as agreed.

Proposed draft clause (for counsel):
"""
Notification & Cooperation: Redwood will notify the Controller without undue delay and, where feasible, no later than seventy-two (72) hours after Redwood becomes aware of a confirmed security incident affecting Controller’s Personal Data. For purposes of this clause, "becomes aware" means the time Redwood’s security team reasonably confirms that Personal Data has been accessed, disclosed, or otherwise compromised. Redwood will, to the extent lawful, cooperate with the Controller and any competent supervisory authority in related investigations and provide an initial evidence package (audit logs, activity summaries, and other prioritized artifacts) within ten (10) business days of notification. If Redwood is required by applicable law or a binding order to delay notification or disclosure to law enforcement, Redwood will notify the Controller of the request to the extent not prohibited by law and will cooperate to the extent permitted. Additional forensic artifacts may require more time; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to agree on timelines for follow‑on evidence production.
"""

We have a couple small optional edits: replace "where feasible" with "as promptly as reasonably practicable" to avoid an impression of judicial permissiveness, and add a short sentence about log retention (we retain detailed flow/audit logs for 12 months by default for Hosted, subject to Dedicated contracts).

If you want, I can send a redline of your SCCs doc and attach our SOC 2 index and SIG answers.

-rachel

Jordan — following internal review please find (a) a suggested clause you can pass to counsel, (b) a short FAQ on operational interpretation, and (c) attached artifacts (SIG answers excerpt, SOC 2 evidence index, SCCs redline).

A) Suggested clause (finalized wording we prefer):
"""
Notification & Cooperation: Redwood will notify the Controller as promptly as reasonably practicable and, in any event, no later than seventy‑two (72) hours after Redwood reasonably becomes aware of a confirmed security incident affecting Controller’s Personal Data. For purposes of this clause, Redwood reasonably becomes aware when its security team, during routine monitoring or triage, determines that there is credible evidence of an incident that has resulted in unauthorized access to, disclosure of, or loss of Personal Data. Redwood will, to the extent not prohibited by applicable law, cooperate with the Controller and the appropriate supervisory authorities and provide an initial evidence package (audit logs, activity summaries, and other prioritized artifacts) within ten (10) business days of notification. Redwood may require additional time to produce extensive forensic artifacts; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to agree on milestones for any follow‑on evidence production.

Where Redwood is subject to a binding legal prohibition (for example, a law enforcement preservation order), Redwood will notify the Controller of the existence of such a prohibition to the extent permitted.
"""

B) Operational FAQ (short):
- "Becomes aware": generally means confirmed by our security triage team; we monitor alerts and may begin investigation earlier, but formal notification starts once data impact is reasonably confirmed.
- Initial evidence package: includes time-stamped audit logs (redacted as necessary), connection/activity summaries, and a high-level incident timeline.
- Retention: Hosted default logs retained 12 months; Dedicated customers can negotiate extended retention.
- Law enforcement: We will notify controllers of requests unless prohibited. If we must delay, we will provide status updates as allowed.

C) Attachments: SIG-Questionnaire-Redwood-Fill.pdf (excerpt), SCCs-redline-draft.docx, evidence-index-soc2.csv

If this works for counsel, we can sign off quickly. Happy to tweak language if your legal team requests.

Best,
